segments.t: Projects save and restore your complete workspace state—all open windows, tabs, SSH connections, and terminal sessions. This lets you quickly switch between different work contexts without manually reconnecting or repositioning windows.
Open KTPH004File KTPH014 Save ProjectKTPH005 or press KTPH006KTPH000KTPH007+KTPH008KTPH001KTPH009 (KTPH010KTPH002KTPH011+KTPH012KTPH003KTPH013 on macOS).
Enter a KTPH000nameKTPH001 and optional KTPH002descriptionKTPH003 for the project.

When enabled, opening the project automatically reconnects every saved terminal and SFTP tab; a tab that needs a password, a new temporary SSH key or the locked vault waits in the KTPH000restore barKTPH001 instead.
When disabled, opening the project restores the windows with their position and size and the local file editor and image viewer tabs only; terminal, SFTP and remote file tabs are skipped.
Projects are KTPH000 files saved wherever you choose in the save dialog, for example in KTPH001.

A project keeps every korTTY window that is open, not only the one you choose KTPH000Save ProjectKTPH001 in; that window is saved first. A window that holds nothing but AI result and tool tabs, which projects do not keep, is left out, so it does not come back empty; the window you save from is always kept, for its position and size.
Open KTPH004File KTPH014 Open ProjectKTPH005 or press KTPH006KTPH000KTPH007+KTPH008KTPH001KTPH009 (KTPH010KTPH002KTPH011+KTPH012KTPH003KTPH013 on macOS).
Select a KTPH000 project file from the file browser.

The project opens right away. File and snippet editors with unsaved changes in the window ask first; then the project replaces the tabs of the window, and every further window saved in the project opens in a new window, see KTPH000WindowsKTPH001.

Opening a project gives its first window to the window you open it from and opens each further window it holds in a new window. Windows that are already open keep their tabs. Projects saved by earlier versions hold only the window they were saved from and open in one window, as before.

KTPH000Position and sizeKTPH001 — each window comes back where it was, with its size, and maximized if it was maximized. When the screen a window was on is no longer attached, the window opens centred on the main screen with its saved size, shrunk to fit if needed. A maximized window keeps the size it had before you maximized it, so un-maximizing it later gives you that size back. Fullscreen is not saved, and the window you open the project from stays in fullscreen if it is.
KTPH000TabsKTPH001 — the tabs come back in their saved order, sorted into their KTPH002tab groupsKTPH003 as usual.

KTPH000Active tabKTPH001 — each window selects the tab that was active when you saved. A remote file editor or image viewer tab opens only once its file has been downloaded; when it was the active tab, the window selects it as soon as it is there, unless you have chosen another tab in the meantime or the download takes longer than 10 seconds. When the active tab does not come back right away, for example because it waits for a password in the KTPH002restore barKTPH003 or its connection was deleted, the window keeps the tab it shows; when you open it from the restore bar later, the window selects it then.
KTPH000DashboardKTPH001 — each window shows or hides the dashboard as it did when you saved.
KTPH000Without Auto-ReconnectKTPH001 the windows open as well, with their local file editor and image viewer tabs; a window whose tabs were all skipped opens empty.
A project opens at most 32 windows; a project file with more, which korTTY writes only when that many windows were open, opens its first 32.
KTPH000File → Open RecentKTPH001 takes you back to what you used last without the file dialog or the Connection Manager:

KTPH001ConnectionsKTPH002 — the saved connections you used last, up to 10, the one used last first: the same connections as the buttons at the top of Quick Connect, which count what you open from Quick Connect, the KTPH003command paletteKTPH004, KTPH005Open GroupKTPH006 and this menu (a connection opened from the Connection Manager is not counted). Each entry shows the connection's name and KTPH000. Choosing one opens a tab for it that signs in like KTPH007ConnectKTPH008 in the Connection Manager (see KTPH009Signing inKTPH010), with the KTPH011server access policyKTPH012 checked first, and counts as a use, so the connection moves to the top.

KTPH003ProjectsKTPH004 — the project files you opened or saved last, up to 10, newest first, followed by the other KTPH000 files in KTPH001, the one changed last first. Each entry shows the file name and its folder, with your home folder written as KTPH002. Choosing one opens the project like KTPH005File → Open Project…KTPH006: editors with unsaved changes ask first, the project replaces the tabs of the window, and further windows saved in it open in new windows. A project file that was moved or deleted is left out of the menu.
KTPH000Clear ListKTPH001 empties the menu. It deletes no connection and no project file: a connection comes back once you use it again, a project once you open or save it.

The menu is rebuilt every time you open the KTPH000FileKTPH001 menu. On macOS, where korTTY keeps running after you close its last window, choosing an entry from the menu bar opens it in a new window.

korTTY keeps the paths of your recent projects, and the time you last chose KTPH001Clear ListKTPH002, in its settings file KTPH000 (see KTPH003Configuration filesKTPH004). They are therefore part of every KTPH005configuration backupKTPH006 and come back when you restore one. Only the paths are kept, never the content of a project, and the connections are not stored a second time: the list follows when each saved connection was last used.

While korTTY runs, it keeps a snapshot of your open windows and tabs, so you get them back after a restart or a crash without saving a project first. At startup korTTY offers them in a bar (see KTPH000At startupKTPH001), and KTPH002File → Restore Previous SessionKTPH003 opens the windows and tabs korTTY had open before this start.

KTPH000When it is savedKTPH001 — a couple of seconds after every change to the windows and tabs: a tab opened, closed, moved, renamed or split, a window opened, closed, moved or resized, the dashboard shown or hidden. When you quit korTTY, or close its last window on Windows and Linux, the snapshot is written once more while every tab is still open, so it holds all the windows you had, although they close one after another while korTTY quits.

KTPH000What it holdsKTPH001 — the same as a project with KTPH002Auto-ReconnectKTPH003 (see KTPH004What Gets SavedKTPH005): every window with its position and size, its tabs in their order with their tab groups, names, split panes, font sizes and terminal effects, SFTP Manager tabs with their folders, file editor and image viewer tabs, and the active tab and the dashboard of each window. Tabs that still wait in the KTPH006restore barKTPH007 or for their remote file are kept too, at their places, and so are the split panes of a restored tab that has not connected yet.
KTPH000What it never holdsKTPH001 — screen text, scrollback, command timestamps, passwords and temporary SSH keys. Each tab names its saved connection by id, as in a project.

KTPH000A session without tabs keeps the last oneKTPH001 — when no tab is open, for example after you closed the last window on macOS, where korTTY keeps running, the snapshot keeps the windows it had and takes only the new Recently Closed list.

KTPH000Restore Previous SessionKTPH001 opens the previous session like a project with Auto-Reconnect and asks nothing while it opens the tabs: a local shell, SSH key authentication, a saved password and a temporary SSH key that is still valid open right away, and every tab that needs a password, a new temporary SSH key or the locked vault waits in the KTPH002restore barKTPH003, where a blocked server or a deleted connection is listed as well. Its first window opens in the window you choose the command in when that window has no tabs, and in a new window otherwise; every further window opens in a new window, and the windows that are open keep their tabs. The command is greyed out while there is no previous session, and after you restored it once, so no tab opens twice.

The previous session is the last one in which korTTY had tabs open: at every start, korTTY makes the session of the last run the previous one, but only when it had at least one tab. A start at which you open nothing therefore never pushes your previous session out.

The KTPH000Recently ClosedKTPH001 list is kept in the same snapshot, so it survives a restart. It keeps only the id of each closed tab's saved connection, with the tab group, the name and the terminal effect: after a restart a closed tab reopens with the saved connection as it is then, and a tab whose connection was deleted, or was never saved (a Quick Connect session), is no longer listed.

korTTY keeps the snapshots in KTPH000 (see KTPH001Configuration filesKTPH002), readable only by you. They describe the windows of this computer and are not part of a KTPH003configuration backupKTPH004. A second korTTY started while the first one runs neither saves its session nor moves the previous one, so the two never write over each other; it can still restore the previous session. While a restored backup with another master password waits for the restart, korTTY saves nothing.

When korTTY starts and the session before this start had at least one tab, a bar above the status line of the window offers it, for example KTPH000Restore the windows and tabs from before this start? Windows: 2, tabs: 6KTPH001. The bar never blocks the window, and nothing opens until you choose:
KTPH000RestoreKTPH001 opens the previous session like KTPH002File → Restore Previous SessionKTPH003.

KTPH000DismissKTPH001 hides the bar and leaves the window as it is. KTPH002File → Restore Previous SessionKTPH003 still opens the session in this run, but the next start does not offer it again; if you open tabs yourself, they are the session the next start offers.
If you do neither and open no tab yourself, the snapshot keeps the offered session, so the next start offers it again, also after a crash.
KTPH000Settings → Window → KTPH001Session RestoreKTPH002KTPH003 chooses what happens at startup:
Offer to restore the previous session (default)

Restores the previous session by itself as soon as no dialog is open, for example once you answered the question about KTPH000anonymous dataKTPH001, so the questions its connections may ask (a host key, a password, an access reason) never come on top of another dialog. If a dialog stays open for a minute, korTTY shows the bar instead.
Shows nothing; KTPH000File → Restore Previous SessionKTPH001 opens the previous session when you want it.

The automatic restore asks nothing that KTPH000Restore Previous SessionKTPH001 would not: tabs that need a password, a new temporary SSH key or the locked vault wait in the KTPH002restore barKTPH003. If korTTY ends without quitting normally within a minute of restoring a session (a crash, a forced quit or a power cut), the next start shows the bar instead of restoring automatically and says that korTTY ended unexpectedly after the last restore, so a session that makes korTTY crash cannot do so at every start. A second korTTY started while the first one runs never offers or restores the session.
A project captures the complete state of your workspace:
Every open korTTY window with its position and size, and whether it was maximized (see KTPH000WindowsKTPH001)

All terminal tabs in each window, including their KTPH000split panesKTPH001 with the server of each pane and the position of every divider, and the name of a KTPH002renamed tabKTPH003, plus SFTP Manager tabs with the local and remote folders they show, and file editor and image viewer tabs
A reference to the saved connection of each tab, by the connection's internal id, so renaming a connection does not break the project
Whether the dashboard was shown, in each window
Which tab was active in each window, by the tab's session id, so it is found again after the tabs were sorted into their groups
The last visible screen of each terminal tab's primary pane — not its scrollback and not the cursor position; the screens of further split panes are not saved

AI result tabs and tool tabs (managers opened as tabs) are not saved with projects. They remain only in the current session and are lost when you close the tab or open a project. SFTP Manager tabs are not tool tabs in this sense: they are saved, see KTPH000SFTP Manager tabsKTPH001.
When KTPH000Auto-ReconnectKTPH001 is enabled, KorTTY automatically:
Restores all windows with their saved position and size, see KTPH000WindowsKTPH001
Reconnects each SSH tab using the original connection settings, and opens each local shell tab again

Opens every tab that can sign in without asking — a local shell, SSH key authentication, a saved password, or a temporary SSH key that is still valid — and lists the others in one bar above the status line, see KTPH000Tabs that wait for youKTPH001
Gives each renamed terminal tab its name back; a tab you never renamed shows the connection's current name

Shows each terminal tab's saved screen dimmed above the new session, framed by a KTPH000Restored output fromKTPH001 row with the date the project was saved and an KTPH002End of restored outputKTPH003 row. The text is written into the local terminal only and is never sent to the server: it does not reach the remote shell or its command history, and a session journal that starts with the connection does not record it (a journal you switch on later imports the scrollback, which then includes the restored rows). Control characters and escape sequences are removed from it before it is shown.
Brings back each terminal tab's split panes once the tab is connected, see KTPH000Split panesKTPH001
Reopens each SFTP Manager tab at the local and remote folders it showed when the project was saved
Selects the active tab of each window and shows or hides its dashboard as saved

If KTPH000Auto-ReconnectKTPH001 is disabled, terminal tabs are not restored: opening the project opens the saved windows at their position and size and reopens local file editor and image viewer tabs, while terminal, SFTP and remote file tabs are skipped. Open those connections again from the Connection Manager.

With KTPH000Auto-ReconnectKTPH001, opening a project asks you nothing while it opens the tabs. Each terminal, SFTP Manager and remote file tab signs in like KTPH002ConnectKTPH003 in the Connection Manager (see KTPH004Signing inKTPH005), but only with what is stored, and your organization's KTPH006server access policyKTPH007 is checked first:

KTPH000Opens right awayKTPH001 — a local shell, SSH key authentication, a password saved in the connection or in its credential, and a temporary SSH key that is still valid. A local shell opens whatever its authentication field says.

KTPH000Waits for youKTPH001 — a password that is not saved, a temporary SSH key that has expired or that the locked vault still keeps encrypted, and a password that is in the locked vault. A temporary key is never renewed without asking.
KTPH000Listed onlyKTPH001 — a server or jump server the server access policy blocks, a connection that was deleted or never saved (a Quick Connect session), and a local file that no longer exists.

The tabs that do not open are listed in one bar above the status line of their window, for example KTPH000Tabs not reopened: sign-in needed (2) · vault locked (1) · blocked by policy (1)KTPH001, instead of a dialog for each tab. The bar never blocks the window, so you can work in the tabs that opened and come back to it later.

Asks for what each waiting tab needs, one tab after the other: its password, a new temporary SSH key, or — for a password in the vault — KTPH000Unlock Vault…KTPH001, where declining asks for the password instead. You are asked once per connection: the other waiting tabs of that connection open with the same answer. KTPH002CancelKTPH003 stops; that tab and the ones after it stay in the bar. The server access policy is checked again before each question, and a server it now blocks, or a connection deleted in the meantime, moves to that part of the list without a dialog.

Shown while tabs wait for the locked vault. Once you have entered the master password, those tabs open, in every window. Unlocking the vault any other way, for example with KTPH000Configuration KTPH002 Security KTPH003 Unlock Vault…KTPH001, opens them as well; a tab whose password turns out not to be in the vault then waits for sign-in instead.

Lists every tab of the bar with its name and why it did not open, for example KTPH000web-01: needs a passwordKTPH001 or KTPH002prod: not allowed by your organization's policy (prod.example.com:22)KTPH003. Choosing a tab that waits for you connects just that tab; blocked and missing tabs are greyed out.
Hides the bar and forgets its tabs.

A tab opened from the bar comes back like the tabs that opened right away: with its saved screen, tab group, name, font size and KTPH000split panesKTPH001, sorted into its tab group. When it was the active tab of the window, the window selects it. Opening another project in the window replaces the bar with the new project's, and closing the window discards it.

With KTPH000Auto-ReconnectKTPH001, a terminal tab that had split panes gets them back once its own session is connected: the panes open one after the other in the background, without a KTPH002ConnectingKTPH003 dialog for each, every pane in the place it had, and the dividers move to where they were when you saved the project. This happens once each time you open the project; when the tab reconnects later, its panes are not added again.

A pane that ran on the tab's connection signs in like the tab, with the same password or SSH key. The KTPH000access reasonKTPH001 you gave for the tab is sent for these panes as well, so a CyberArk-style server asks only once. A host key question and the prompts of a keyboard-interactive sign-in still appear when the server asks.

A pane you had opened with KTPH000Split Right (new connection)KTPH001 or KTPH002Split Down (new connection)KTPH003, and the panes split from it on the same server, open on that pane's saved connection, not on the tab's server. They sign in only with what is stored: the SSH key, or the password from the Credentials manager or the connection. Here korTTY does not ask for a password or a new temporary SSH key and does not offer to unlock the vault.
Every pane passes your organization's KTPH000server access policyKTPH001, the panes on the tab's own server included, because a saved connection may have been changed since the project was saved.

A pane that cannot open stays closed together with the panes that were split from it, and the other panes keep their places. That happens when the pane needs a password or a new temporary SSH key, when the vault is locked, when the policy does not allow its server, when its connection was deleted or never saved (a Quick Connect session), or when the connection fails. The status bar then says how many panes of which tab were not reopened and why, for example KTPH000web-01: 2 of 4 split panes were not reopened (vault locked)KTPH001. Open them again with KTPH002Split RightKTPH003 or KTPH004Split DownKTPH005.
At most 32 panes per tab are reopened; a project file with more, which korTTY never writes itself, opens with the first 32.
Projects saved by earlier versions do not store a server for each pane: all their panes open on the tab's server, as before.

With KTPH000Auto-ReconnectKTPH001, each saved SFTP Manager tab connects to its connection again and opens the local and remote folders it showed when you saved the project. Without KTPH002Auto-ReconnectKTPH003, SFTP Manager tabs are not reopened.
A local folder that no longer exists opens your home folder instead.

A remote folder that no longer exists opens your login directory on the server, and the status bar says KTPH000Remote folderKTPH001 KTPH002pathKTPH003 KTPH004no longer exists; showing the home folderKTPH005. A remote folder that exists but cannot be read, for example for lack of rights, shows the usual error and opens the login directory as well.

Projects saved by earlier versions referred to SFTP Manager tabs by the connection's name. Such a tab is still restored when exactly one connection has that name; when several connections share the name, the tab is skipped and the log says why. Save the project again to store the reference by id.

A remote image viewer tab is saved with the connection it was opened from, even when several SFTP Manager tabs are open or its SFTP Manager tab is already closed. When restored, it opens its own SFTP connection, with the same SSH key and jump server as the SFTP Manager, and that connection closes when you close the tab.

A saved file editor tab opens its file again: a local file when it still exists, and — with KTPH000Auto-ReconnectKTPH001 — a remote file over an SFTP connection of its own, which closes when you close the tab. The project stores which file was open, not its unsaved changes.

A file editor tab with unsaved changes shows KTPH000 after its name, and every way of closing it asks KTPH005SaveKTPH006, KTPH007DiscardKTPH008 or KTPH009CancelKTPH010 first: the tab's close button, the editor's KTPH011CloseKTPH012 button or KTPH013KTPH001KTPH014+KTPH015KTPH002KTPH016 (KTPH017KTPH003KTPH018+KTPH019KTPH004KTPH020 on macOS) in the editor, KTPH021File KTPH029 Close TabKTPH022, KTPH023File KTPH030 Close All TabsKTPH024, opening a project, closing the window and quitting korTTY. KTPH025CancelKTPH026 keeps the tab open; when the question came from KTPH027Close All TabsKTPH028, opening a project or closing the window, nothing is closed. If saving fails, for example because the SFTP connection is gone, korTTY shows the error and keeps the tab open with your changes. When several tabs have unsaved changes, korTTY selects each one before it asks about it.
A project is a plain XML file with the KTPH000 extension. Each project includes:
Every window with its position, size and tabs, and the session id of its active tab
Connection references (by connection id, so the connection must exist in your Connection Manager)

The saved screen text is not part of the KTPH000 file. It is stored separately as one gzip file per terminal tab, KTPH001, which the project references by file name — a project file you share therefore carries the layout but not the screen text. korTTY only ever reads, writes or deletes plain file names inside KTPH002; a project whose reference points anywhere else opens without that screen text.

A project file never carries a pane's working directory or a reference to saved scrollback: korTTY removes both from every project it opens or saves, so a project someone sends you cannot choose the folder a local shell starts in or point a pane at a file.
